doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Oral history, C-Span and the end of tyranny
summary: Praises living history and says politicians and the Republican party are finished.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah sure. I think these things are important. I think what you’re doing is important. I think that younger students especially need to feel some contact with people they may never have seen in their lifetimes, but whom, if they’re studying jazz, have an impact on them. That’s the value of this. It’s like a volume of history, but it’s living history. These kinds of things are going to supercede history books. I don’t think there’ll be history books far into the future, especially if people write history as it occurs instead of waiting for years after the event has passed so that they can lie safely, you know, and also waiting until interest in it has waned. I think history should be written contemporarily, like you’re doing with this. We should do the same thing politically. C-Span is actually doing that. C-Span is taking you into the House of Representatives, into the Senate, and showing you these great and noble souls that are supposed to defend the rights of you, the people. And what you get to see is just how little they do that, and how mealy mouthed they are about defending the rights of those who pay them, like the National Rifle Association and the tobacco interests and the National Association of Manufacturers. Those are their true sponsors and the people to whom they give their true worth as representatives of the people. And the people have seen this, have seen it over and over again. They’ve listened to Orrin Hatch try to justify the fact that he is humane enough to run for president while citing the fact that, “I have many Jewish friends — I have this 92-year old lady who is a Jewish lady, a very good friend of mine.” The man killed himself. To any person listening and looking on, he killed himself. You condescending bastard. But he did it himself. Nobody else did it. And the people are watching them every day, kill themselves. The Republican party is dead. They’re dead in the water. They don’t even know it. If you blow on them, they’ll fall down, bam. They are so decrepit, so inhumane, so out of touch with where people really are at. People who suffer from racism don’t even want any more. They say come on, man. You know these kids today, they’re saying hey come on man. Come on, let’s get together, let’s go. They’re transcending all that stuff. That’s garbage. That stuff is finished. But these people still think there’s nobody looking at them, there’s nobody listening to them. Look at Pinochet. Pinochet would have gotten off the English lords would have let him off. They had no documentary information. So what did they do? They punched up Uruguay on the internet, and there came all his crimes. The internet has abolished tyranny. Tyranny is finished. It’s done.
Because everybody will know about it.

Everybody will know about it the minute you think of it. So we’re living in a marvelous time here. And the changes are incalculable, and the ideas you have about everything are passe. Even whatever you can think of uttering, it’s already passe, gone. Because you’re © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -20-
either going to go forward or you’re going to go backwards. And if you go backwards you’re going to fall off.
